key_insight: US clinical trials that require English proficiency enroll fewer Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants, while language accommodation is uncommon.
clinical_relevance: Adding or removing language eligibility criteria is a modifiable trial-design feature that could affect who gets represented in clinical research.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of 44,487 interventional ClinicalTrials.gov trials with exclusively US sites and posted results.
Free-text eligibility criteria were classified for English-language requirements and language accommodation using validated regular expressions.
Adjusted generalized linear models tested associations with enrolled racial/ethnic composition and trial/site characteristics.
evidence_signal: The English-language requirement classifier was validated against physician review with 88.2% sensitivity and 99.2% specificity, and the study found the requirement in 12.9% of trials versus language accommodation in 1.8%.
watch_item: These are observational registry data, so the findings show association rather than proof that language criteria alone caused the enrollment differences.
paper_title: Language eligibility criteria and enrolled racial and ethnic composition in US clinical trials: a cross-sectional study
